In [[probability theory]], a '''Fleming–Viot process (F–V process)''' is a member of a particular subset of [[probability measure]]-valued [[Markov process]]es on [[compact space|compact]] [[metric space]]s, as defined in the 1979 paper by [[Wendell Fleming|Wendell Helms Fleming]] and Michel Viot. Such processes are [[Martingale (probability theory)|martingales]] and [[Diffusion process|diffusions]].

The Fleming–Viot processes have proved to be important to the development of a mathematical basis for the theories behind [[Genetic drift|allele drift]].
They are generalisations of the Wright–Fisher process and arise as infinite population limits of suitably rescaled variants of [[Moran process]]es.
